title: Grade 4 Social Studies — Native Nations, Places, and Living Cultures
subject: Social Studies
description: Practice with questions on tribal sovereignty, Haudenosaunee, Shawnee, Myaamia.
creator: Teach Arcade

questions.question: Why is it more accurate to name a specific Native nation when describing its traditions?
choices: Native nations never share any traditions.
All nations speak the same language.
Different nations have distinct histories and practices.
A tradition cannot belong to a living community.

questions.question: Which is true of many Native nations today?
choices: They only appear in historical stories.
They no longer teach their languages.
They have their own governments and living cultures.
They all share one government for every nation.

questions.question: Which is the best primary choice for learning how a Native nation describes its own culture today?
choices: a movie with no named nation
an old toy label
materials shared by that nation's cultural office
a travel flyer without sources

questions.question: What does tribal sovereignty include?
choices: the idea that every nation uses identical laws
a Native nation's authority to govern itself
a rule making every community a museum
control of all foreign governments

questions.question: Why might Native people describe the same river in more than one language?
choices: Communities can have different languages and histories in a place.
A river's name always comes from maps published today.
Each river can have only one name.
A language cannot describe natural places.

questions.question: Which name refers to a confederacy of Native nations also known as the Six Nations?
choices: Thirteen Colonies
Haudenosaunee Confederacy
Ohio General Assembly
United States Congress

questions.question: Which nation works with the Myaamia Center to support the Myaamia language and culture?
choices: Miami Tribe of Oklahoma
Navajo Nation
Cherokee Nation
Osage Nation

questions.question: Why do some Native communities support language programs?
choices: to replace every language in the world
to help people learn and use their language across generations
to make books impossible to read
to keep people from speaking to their elders

questions.question: Which source best shows that Native culture continues in the present?
choices: an unlabeled drawing made by a tourist long ago
a blank timeline ending in 1800
a recent interview with a Native artist about their current work
a sign with no date or author

questions.question: What did the historic earthworks in Ohio require their builders to do?
choices: use printed road signs from modern cities
organize and plan large building projects
wait for European machines to arrive
live without measuring space

questions.question: Which label accurately describes a group with historic connections to the Ohio River region?
choices: Shawnee people
all French-speaking communities
every Native nation in North America
the British Parliament

questions.question: If a museum label uses one word for all Native cultures, what is a good improvement?
choices: remove the item's date and place
change all names to “unknown” even when they are known
identify the nation and explain the item's own context
label every object with the same maker

questions.question: Why can comparing historical housing designs show adaptation?
choices: Every nation had identical weather and resources.
Homes show nothing about how people live.
All houses were temporary everywhere.
Different resources and climates can shape different designs.

questions.question: Which is a good way to handle a story that a community shares only in certain settings?
choices: follow the community's guidance
say the community has no stories
post it publicly without asking
write a different ending and call it original

questions.question: What is one reason to study Native nations both before and after early contact with Europeans?
choices: It keeps you from noticing change over time.
It shows every nation had the same experience.
It proves each nation stopped existing at first contact.
It shows histories that began earlier and continued through change.

questions.question: What can a territory map and a present-day nation website show together?
choices: historic places and present-day community life
exactly what every person in history thought
that communities have no ties to land
why all Native nations share one language

questions.question: Which is an example of cultural knowledge that can be passed down?
choices: what all people must eat on the same day
a random list of street numbers with no context
a rule that all nations tell the same stories
how and when to gather a food safely in a certain place

questions.question: What does a treaty show best on its own?
choices: whether everyone freely agreed to it
that both sides always followed it
how everyone felt about it
what a written agreement says

questions.question: What could a school group do before using a design linked to a Native nation?
choices: say it belongs to every nation
learn its purpose through sources from the nation and ask about permission
use it for any purpose without checking
copy it and invent a meaning

questions.question: Which is an accurate way to describe Native nations?
choices: They belong only in the past.
They all have identical ways of choosing leaders.
They formed only after the U.S. became a country.
They have changed over time while maintaining distinct identities.
